Read about the data from the website where it is staged.  

Form three regression models; 
  Model1 is mpg~disp, 
  Model2 is mge~hp, and 
  Model3 is mpg~disp+hp. 
  
For each model find a 95% prediction interval of the mpg given a value of 183 for disp GRIP and 250 for hp 

After all three models have been constructed, compare Model1 with Model3 using anova. Document the comparison the markdown document, 

As usual, push the project up to your github account and submit the URL to canvas as link. 

 


```{r include=FALSE}
require(tidyverse)
require(tigerstats)
require(rgl)
require(knitr)
library(MASS)
```

```{r}
data(mtcars)
myData = mtcars

```

## Model 1 mpg ~ disp

### scatterplot

```{r}
plot(mpg~disp,data=mtcars,pch=19)
```
This scatter plot shows the relationship between displacement and miles per gallon, a negative correlation skewed to the right. As the displacement increases the miles per gallon  decreases.  
### Numerical results
```{r}
cor(mpg~disp,data=mtcars)
```

The correlation coefficient between mgp and disp is -0.85. As the car engines displacement increases the mpg decreases significantly. 
### Inferential  (Build model.1)
```{r}
model.1 <- lm(mpg~disp,data=mtcars)
summary.lm(model.1)
```
For every unit increase in the cars displacement the cars mpg is predicted to decrease by approximately 0.041215 units. The model is significantly significant. 

#### Predict at target point
```{r}

newdata=data.frame(disp=183,hp=250)
predict(model.1,newdata)
```
predicted mpg 

## Model 2 mgp~hp

```{r}
plot(mpg~hp,data=mtcars,pch=19)
```
This scatter plot displays the strong negative relationship between the mpg and the hp.The data is right-skewed. As the cars hp increases, its mgp decreases. 
### Numerical results 2
```{r}
cor(mtcars$mpg,mtcars$hp)
```
The correlation coefficient is -0.776 which meaans there is a strong linear relationship, as the horsepower increases the mpg decrease. 

### Inferential  (Build model.2)
```{r}
model.2 <- lm(mpg~hp,data=mtcars)
summary.lm(model.2)
```
For every 1 unit of hp you add the mpg drop by about 0.07 units.

#### predict model.2 at target point
```{r}

predict(model.2,newdata)
```
For every cubic inch increase in engine size means you get about this much mpg (13.04179)
